Subject: ProdLytics onboarding: cost/perf tuning handoff & next steps

Emma —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move into the implementation phase I want to loop you in on the specific cost/performance tuning activities our CS + Implementation team will run during the first 4 weeks. Attaching the ProdLytics_kpis_v1.pdf and a draft handoff checklist.

Quick summary of what we'll cover in the kickoff & first sprint:
- Baseline traffic profile (qps, avg sequence length, peak windows) — please confirm if the sample in the KPI doc is representative.
- Batching strategy options: autopool vs fixed-window; target latency SLOs for p95 and p99.
- KV/prefix caching candidates and TTL expectations.
- Quantization profiles to evaluate (we'll start with medium-int8 and a float16 fallback).
- Routing policy: initial single-region production with cross-region fallback; cost-tier routing if throughput spikes.

Can you confirm the baseline QPS and a sample payload with expected sequence lengths? Also let us know if there are contractual constraints around token retention or caching (we can honor short TTLs if needed).

Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff call: Tue 6/17 — 30 minutes (technical + CS).
2) Exchange a small sample of production traces (anonymized).
3) Redwood runs a 48-hour synthetic load with your sample to gather baseline cost & latency metrics.

I assigned Sean to run the orchestration checklist and Grace to draft quant/profile recommendations. Karthik will help with client-side changes for batching.

Attachments:
- ProdLytics_kpis_v1.pdf (pdf)
- handoff-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks —

Monica —

Thanks for the clear outline. A few items to confirm from ProdLytics side:
- Baseline: steady-state ~12 QPS, daily peak ~85 QPS for 20–30 minute windows; average prompt length 280 tokens, responses ~160 tokens.
- We can provide anonymized traces (Nginx + app logs) and a 5% sample of actual payloads (PII removed).
- Caching: we can allow prefix caching for system prompts and stable reference prompts, TTL up to 24 hours. Cannot cache user PII.
- Quantization: we'd prefer to start conservative (float16) and only move to int8 if quality checks pass — but open to Redwood's recommendations based on test metrics.

Kickoff on Tue 6/17 works. Can you propose a time? We prefer mornings PST.

Attaching a short internal doc with the traffic windows and current infra.

Best,

- Quant profiles to try: float16 baseline, medium-int8 profile A, conservative int8 profile B. (Owner: Grace)
- Routing policy draft: primary-region (us-west1) + fallback to us-central if latency > threshold or capacity events. (Owner: Karthik)

I'll attach the synthetic plan and the cost-estimation spreadsheet to the shared Drive after this thread. For the kickoff, Grace — can you bring the proposed quant_profiles.yml sample and a quick note on expected quality delta vs tokens saved?

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ProdLytics onboarding: cost/perf tuning handoff & next steps

Following up with the technical checklist and initial recommendations so the kickoff is productive. Below are my notes — copying into the kickoff doc as well.

Baseline assumptions (from ProdLytics): avg seq = 440 tokens total, peak 85 QPS. We'll design tests around those numbers.

1) Batching
- Proposal: client-side micro-batching at 40ms aggregation for p95-sensitive endpoints; server-side continuous batching for high-throughput endpoints with target batch-size cap of 32 tokens. Rationale: preserve sub-350ms p95 while getting batching benefits for throughput.

2) Caching
- Candidate prefixes: system prompts + top 8 static templates (Emma will confirm list). TTL default 6h, configurable up to 24h per ProdLytics note. We'll hash and anonymize payload keys before applying prefix cache.

3) Quantization profiles
- Attached proposed_quant_profiles.yml includes three profiles: fp16-safe, med-int8 (aggressive medium), int8-conservative. Testing matrix: run A/B on med-int8 and fp16 with 10k sample prompts; evaluate BLEU-style and business quality checks.

4) Routing policy
- Draft policy: route to us-west1 unless GPU queue depth > 70% for >30s or p95 latency breaches 350ms -> failover to us-central with cost-tier fallback enabled (lower-cost model variant).

5) Quality gates & rollout
- Canary: 5% traffic med-int8 vs fp16 for 48 hours. If quality delta < 1.5% on classification/regression metrics and no user-facing errors, expand to 25% then 100%.

Next steps for kickoff:
- Monica: upload traces + KPI doc to drive link.
- Emma: confirm prefix list and sample payloads delivered.
- Sean: run synthetic plan and share results.

Attachments to be uploaded after kickoff: proposed_quant_profiles.yml, handoff-checklist.xlsx, synthetic-load-plan.csv

Grace O'Connor
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
